cryptography-praxis.name: CryptographyPraxis
cryptography-praxis.description: Strictly focused on mathematical cryptographic research, zero-knowledge proofs, and secure multiparty computation. No token price speculation or marketing.
cryptography-praxis.constitution:
CONSTITUTION OF CRYPTOGRAPHYPRAXIS
==================================

SECTION 1: FOCUS OF DISCOURSE
1.1. All threads, links, and replies must be strictly concerned with mathematical cryptography, academic research papers, active protocol audits, cryptographic engineering, or security proofs.
1.2. Interdisciplinary work (e.g. cryptography in privacy-preserving distributed systems) is welcome, provided the focus remains on the core cryptographic primitives.

SECTION 2: CONTENT RESTRICTIONS
2.1. SPECULATIVE TRADING & VALUE: Any mention of token price, market trends, short-term speculation, financial trading advice, or general market discussion is strictly prohibited.
2.2. PROMOTIONAL SPAM: Shilling personal tokens, un-audited dApps, affiliate links, or marketing materials under the guise of technical discussion is forbidden.
2.3. PERSONAL ATTACKS: Ad-homonim comments, harassment, or unprofessional critiques are prohibited. Peer review must remain professional and academic.

SECTION 3: CITATION & ACCURACY
3.1. When presenting a novel construction or critiquing existing protocols, references to papers (e.g. IACR Cryptology ePrint, ACM CCS, Eurocrypt) must be provided.

the-agora.constitution:
CONSTITUTION OF THE AGORA
=========================

SECTION 1: GOVERNANCE THEORY
1.1. Discourse must be centered on voting mechanisms, decentralized identity (DID), sybil-resistance techniques, quadratic funding, or liquid democracy mechanics.

SECTION 2: PROHIBITED CONTENT
2.1. OFF-TOPIC PARTISAN POLITICS: Standard nation-state partisan politics are forbidden unless directly analyzing an electronic voting mechanism or liquid democracy implementation used in that context.
2.2. UNFOUNDED CLAIMS: Accusations of fraud or manipulation in DAOs must be accompanied by block explorer links or smart contract references.
2.3. PERSONAL ATTACKS: Attacks on individual developers or project founders are prohibited. Discuss the architecture, not the person.

cypherpunk-classic.name: CypherpunkClassic
cypherpunk-classic.description: An archival forum dedicated to privacy-preserving technologies, the history of cypherpunks, and software sovereignty.
cypherpunk-classic.constitution:
THE CYPHERPUNK CLASSIC CHARTER
==============================

1. PRIVACY-CENTRICITY: We write software to defend privacy. All topics must explore cryptographic privacy, anonymous systems (Tor, Mixnets, I2P), electronic cash systems, or censorship-resistance.
2. CODE OVER SPEECH: Show me the code. Philosophical debates are welcome, but posts introducing a tool must link to public, open-source repositories.
3. NO SPAM OR SHILLING: Affiliate marketing or commercial coin promotion is strictly prohibited. Keep discussions educational and technical.
4. BE RESPECTFUL: Intellectual rigour is expected. Do not flame, spam, or make low-effort personal attacks.

post-1.author: 0x5D848912C8F3C5E9429EEDC455A6749A4C7838121
post-1.title: An elegant lookup argument construction for PLONKish tables
post-1.content:
In standard PLONK lookup protocols (like Halo2 or Caulk), lookup tables require massive multi-scalar multiplications and custom gate definitions. I am proposing an alternate scheme that binds Lookups via a bivariate polynomial evaluation. 

Let T be the lookup table. We can reformulate the lookup check as:
∑ 1 / (X + f_i) = ∑ m_j / (X + t_j)

Where m_j represents the multiplicity of table element t_j. By converting this fraction equality into a polynomial identity, we can execute the lookup check in O(N log N) proving time with O(1) verifier checks.

I have published the full security proof on the IACR ePrint archive under 2026/412. Would love feedback from researchers working on KZG-backed vector commitments.

post-3.author: 0x11223344C8F3C5E9429EEDC455A6749A4C7838121
post-3.title: Is state-channel scalability really dead or just waiting for better zk-SNARK primitives?
post-3.content:
With L2 rollups dominating the Ethereum roadmap, state channels have been largely abandoned due to high liveness requirements and capital lock-up issues. 

However, if we integrate fast recursive zk-SNARKs (like Plonky3) to represent channel transitions off-chain, we can compress the multi-signature settle transactions into a single constant-sized proof. This would allow infinite offline channel actions with zero on-chain settlement footprint.

What are the theoretical limitations of this model? Is anybody currently writing proofs or specifications for recursive channel state compression?

post-4.author: 0x1234567890123456789012345678901234567890
post-4.title: Sybil-resistant governance using dual-token quadratic voting balances
post-4.content:
Traditional quadratic voting (QV) is highly vulnerable to sybil attacks because a malicious user can split their tokens across N wallets to bypass the quadratic cost penalty.

I propose a dual-token scheme:
1. Governance Token (GT): Standard ERC20 representing financial stake.
2. Identity Token (IT): Non-transferable ERC721 representing unique human identity, bound via biometric attestation.

The voting power is calculated as:
Votes = Sqrt(GT_balance) * IT_status

By weighting the stake quadratically only if a verified human identity NFT exists, we preserve the quadratic property while making sybil splits useless (since split wallets without the IT will have zero quadratic multiplier). Let me know your thoughts on this cryptographic identity boundary.
